New York Sues Prediction Market Platform Polymarket Over Alleged Illegal Gambling Operations According to Reuters, the State of New York filed a lawsuit on Thursday against decentralized prediction market operator Polymarket, accusing the platform of conducting an illegal gambling operation. The legal action follows related enforcement measures by New York Attorney General Letitia James targeting prediction platforms—including earlier actions against Kalshi, Coinbase, and Gemini—alleging the unlicensed offering of event-based betting within the state. — link

Vitalik Shanghai Speech: Blockchain Needs New Cryptographic Tools Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said blockchain is evolving from a standalone ledger into a broader cryptographic network spanning L1s, L2s, mempools, off-chain computation, and multi-participant block building. As powerful data analysis and AI make the privacy model of early public blockchains increasingly insufficient, technologies such as SNARKs, STARKs, fully homomorphic encryption, and formal verification are becoming key tools for privacy, scalability, and security. Buterin said zero-knowledge technology is moving from long-term roadmaps into concrete EIPs, while AI is accelerating the development and verification of complex cryptographic systems. In the emerging era of “programmable cryptography,” blockchain systems can move beyond determining “who can send what” to determining “who can see what.” — link

Fed Seeks Comment on Two GENIUS Act Stablecoin Proposals The Federal Reserve is seeking public comment on two proposals to establish a regulatory framework for Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act. The first would require stablecoins to be fully backed by eligible reserve assets, including short-term U.S. Treasuries, and set capital, risk-management and reserve-custody requirements while clarifying permissible stablecoin activities for supervised banks. The second would establish a tailored application process for supervised banks seeking to issue payment stablecoins, including requirements to submit business plans and financial information. Comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. — link

Bitget Wallets Suspected of Security Breach, Over $170M in Assets Moved and Swapped to ETH Breaking: MLM monitoring indicates that Bitget may be experiencing an ongoing wallet security incident, with three hot wallets and one cold wallet suspected to have been compromised. More than $170 million worth of assets have reportedly been moved out and swapped into ETH, with activity linked to 0x770b10b273fC44Fe9197D6bF20F145c2e98463Ee. The affected wallets are said to still hold about $530 million in assets. The attack vector and total losses remain unconfirmed, and Bitget has not yet publicly responded. — link
